qa_pairs.question: What does Seun's self-description of her eating habits suggest about where she stood with her dietary identity at that point — and what in how she frames a particular moment reveals it?
qa_pairs.answer: Seun was already holding herself to a vegan standard internally before she formally announced it. In Session 1 she describes eating fish over Christmas as a lapse she regrets ('I did eat more fish than I wanted') and immediately reasserts her plant-based identity ('I am back on strictly plant-based now'). The defensiveness — framing the fish as something that happened to her ('I only slipped') rather than a choice — signals that her self-concept had already shifted to fully plant-based, even if practice had not yet caught up. By Session 3 the health-check results gave her the external confirmation she needed to commit publicly and drop the apologetic framing.

qa_pairs.question: When Seun announces a major change to her approach to food, what does Emeka's response in the group chat reveal about his own position — and what makes his response more telling than an outright objection would have been?
qa_pairs.answer: Emeka's single-word response 'Noted.' to Seun's full vegan announcement signals deliberate closure rather than engagement. Unlike Tolu (who gave clinical advice), Uncle Dele (who offered qualified respect), or Adaeze (who promised to adapt her cooking), Emeka offers nothing except acknowledgment. The word 'Noted' is his established way of ending topics he does not want to discuss further. His follow-up turn in the same session — 'She knows. She has always known. E.' — confirms resignation rather than approval: he accepts that Seun is committed but will not say more. The contrast with his enthusiastic oxtail contribution in Session 2 makes the silence around her dietary identity particularly visible.

qa_pairs.question: What does Nkem's pattern of describing her own experience at family events suggest about her preference for how she engages with the family — and what in the conversation shows she is aware of this about herself?
qa_pairs.answer: Nkem prefers smaller, more intimate settings to large family gatherings. In Session 5 she admits the January gathering was 'a little full-on at first' and separately adds 'a smaller table would suit me better in an ideal world.' The phrase 'in an ideal world' reveals self-awareness: she knows the preference but softens it to avoid seeming ungrateful. Her recovery sentence ('it was genuinely lovely') follows immediately after each admission — a pattern of self-correction that signals the preference is real but she is managing how directly she expresses it within the group.

qa_pairs.answer: Uncle Dele made the shared-experience observation: 'EMEKA I trust you are well. Rest is important at our age. I note the same. Best regards, Dele.' The key phrase is 'at our age' — this positions Dele as a peer of Emeka, someone in the same life stage who speaks from parallel experience, not from clinical training. Tolu made the clinical version later in the same session: 'Clinically speaking, rest after exertion is appropriate. Just to note, Dad — if this is a pattern we should talk.' The distinction: Dele frames rest as peer-wisdom from shared ageing; Tolu frames it as a medical observation with a conditional concern attached. The framing difference is also visible in register — Dele's 'I note the same' is personal endorsement, while Tolu's 'Clinically speaking' is professional distancing.
